fixes.explanation: Not quite. Luke says they thought the kingdom of God would appear “imminently.” (Luke 19:11) That means any minute now, like someone standing at the oven door with the timer still running. Jesus told them this parable because He was near Jerusalem and they thought that.

Bless your generous heart, baker. I'd hand out cookies all day too. But this parable doesn't go there. The man tells his servants, “Conduct business with this until I return…” (Luke 19:13) Nothing in the passage says he sends the money to the poor.

Nope, that's not the message they sent. The text says his subjects hated him, and their message is, “We do not want this man to rule over us.” (Luke 19:14) That's all the delegation says, and the passage says nothing about hurrying him home.

Hold on, baker, this one is true. When the man returns, he summons the servants he gave the money to, to find out what each one earned. He handed out the money, so he wants the report. Same as me checking the cooling rack after a batch, because nobody sneaks a cookie past me.

Close to the neighborhood, but not the house. A later servant lays his mina away in a piece of cloth (Luke 19:20), and the master doesn't praise him for it. This servant is praised because “…you have been faithful in a very small matter…” (Luke 19:17) That's the reason the master gives.

Sounds fancy, and I'd pull up a chair for that table. But the master doesn't say it. His words are, “…you shall have authority over ten cities.” (Luke 19:17) The reward is authority, and it's counted in cities.

Ten is the right number, but it belongs somewhere else. The ten more minas are what the first servant's mina produced (Luke 19:16). The master's reward is, “…you shall have authority over ten cities.” (Luke 19:17) So it's cities, not servants.

I see the mix-up, baker, but these two servants have two different reports. The second servant says, “Master, your mina has made five minas.” (Luke 19:18) Ten more minas was the first servant's report. Easy to blend them together, like two batches that look alike on the cooling rack.

Land is a creative idea, baker, but the master never mentions it. His question is, “Why then did you not deposit my money in the bank, and upon my return I could have collected it with interest?” (Luke 19:23) The bank is the one thing he names. So that's the answer.

Yes. The master says, “Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.” (Luke 19:24) That's the first servant, the one whose mina produced ten more. Those standing by answer that he already has ten (Luke 19:25).

Yes. His subjects hated him and sent a delegation that said, “We do not want this man to rule over us.” (Luke 19:14) The master calls them “…these enemies of mine who were unwilling for me to rule over them…” (Luke 19:27) I think this is a heavy part of the parable, and it's worth slowing down for.
